items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 232

TO THE ASSEMBLY:

I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:

Assembly Bill Number 2417-C, entitled:

    "AN  ACT  to  amend the agriculture and markets law and the New York
      state urban development corporation act, in relation to creating a
      farm investment fund"

    NOT APPROVED

  This bill would require the Department of Agriculture and Markets  and
Empire  State Development to establish a farm investment fund to provide
grants to farmers seeking to make investments in their farms and farming
practices, but unfortunately fails to provide any funding to support it.
Because the Legislature did not appropriate funding  in  the  budget  to
establish such a fund, the bill cannot be effectuated.

  I  full support the intent of this bill and I am committed to support-
ing our State's farmers. This past year  alone,  my  Administration  has
awarded  over  $40  million to support farmers, agritourism, and invest-
ments in preserving and protecting farmland, including:

  $18 million awarded through the Southern  Tier  Agricultural  Industry
Enhancement  Program,  which helps farmers and agribusinesses expand and
improve their  operations,  while  promoting  the  responsible  use  and
protection of the State's natural resources;

  $10.1  million  awarded through the Farmland Protection Implementation
Grant program to nine projects to help protect more than 5,500 acres  of
at-risk  farmland  in  the  Finger Lakes, supporting the preservation of
farmland for agricultural use and protecting it from degradation through
perpetual conservation easements; and

  $1 million awarded to assist new and early-stage farmers  through  the
New York State New Farmers Grant Fund, building upon the success of 2015
when  more  than $743,000 was awarded to 25 early-stage farms across the
State to support the continued growth of New York's  agriculture  indus-
try.

  A  new agricultural assistance program would complement these existing
programs. To ensure that such a program has the appropriate  funding  to
function,  this  proposal  would  be  better addressed during the annual
State Budget negotiations.

  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
